metadata.note: The original Western Pacific Railroad's Sacramento-Oakland line, the true western end of the first transcontinental railroad, now the Capitol Corridor. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Western Pacific Railroad 1862-1870, Alameda Terminal, First transcontinental railroad), cprr.org
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The Western Pacific Railroad (the original 1862 company, unrelated to the later WP of California Zephyr fame) was chartered to build the westernmost link of the first transcontinental railroad. It opened Sacramento-Alameda Sept 6 1869, when the first through train from Sacramento reached San Francisco Bay - completing the transcontinental railroad 'from the Missouri river to the Pacific ocean.' The overland passenger terminus moved from Alameda to the Oakland Pier Nov 8 1869. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
